endpoints.endpointName: Central Avenue public river access (parking-area anchor)
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: nm_cabq_central_avenue_public_access_anchor_20260918 cabq-central-avenue-sunset-sw-parking-access-area: The City identifies public boating access on the north side of the Central Avenue bridge on both river banks, requiring a walk to the river. Its March 2025 notice confirms the bosque parking lot at the southwest corner of Central and the river and says the river access point there would be improved for paddle sports. Quiet Waters publishes the stored coordinate as the Central Avenue Access GPS point after directions to the Sunset SW parking area. Retain it as the public parking/access-area anchor; it is not a surveyed water-entry toe, and users must carry boats to the current landing.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (nm_cabq_central_avenue_public_access_anchor_20260918 cabq-central-avenue-sunset-sw-parking-access-area) on Rio Grande; this confirms the public access site, not the exact water-edge point. Confirm the water-edge location and carry before paddling.

endpoints.reach: Central Avenue access to Rio Bravo Boulevard access
endpoints.endpointName: Rio Bravo Boulevard public river access (access-area anchor)
endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: nm_cabq_rio_bravo_nw_launch_access_anchor_20260918 cabq-rio-bravo-nw-emergency-launch-access-area: The City Open Space assessment distinguishes the northwest-bank Rio Bravo access from the northeast Poco Loco picnic/fishing site: it records informal parking and trails along Kelsey Road, limited access due to bridge expansion, and an emergency launch at the northwest site. The 2025 USACE project notice for NMDOT's bridge replacement includes recontouring an existing boat ramp; 2024 project materials identify a new northwest parking lot and impacts to the boat launch. Construction began in September 2026. Quiet Waters publishes the stored coordinate as the Rio Bravo SW access GPS reference. Keep it as a public launch/access-area anchor, not a surveyed wet-toe point, and treat availability as conditional during bridge construction.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (nm_cabq_rio_bravo_nw_launch_access_anchor_20260918 cabq-rio-bravo-nw-emergency-launch-access-area) on Rio Grande; access is conditional (The City identifies this northwest-bank location as an emergency launch/access area with limited informal parking and trails. The NM 500 bridge replacement is active and includes work on the existing boat ramp. Verify the west-bank gate, launch and carry are open before staging; access and the coordinate may change during construction.), not unrestricted public access. This confirms the managed access area, not the exact water-edge point.
